liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Jerry's guitar kicked back in toward the end of this song after early second-set problems, and the crowd responded; China Cat into Rider was soulful [13][23]
- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): The Bertha into Jack Straw opening was pretty hot; Follows Bertha without a pause, even faster and more effective, making a strong one-two opening punch [15][16]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Mickey produced great thunder sounds at the end; this and He's Gone lifted the show into overdrive [14]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): China Cat into Rider limped along compared with the energy of the following Looks Like Rain and He's Gone [14]
- **Knockin' On Heaven's Door** (1 review): Reviewer, not usually a fan of the song, calls this their all-time favorite version [15]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Opener is fast and breezy, but the solos fail to electrify; sound seemed filtered, as through a veil [16]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Has a steady beat and decent thread; reviewer notes an odd moment after tuning [16]
- **Blow Away** (1 review): Has particularly great energy [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-03-30 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-03-30 t02 Bertha**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-03-30 t03 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-03-30 t04 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-03-30 t05 Blow Away**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-03-30 t06 When I Paint My Masterpiece**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-03-30 t07 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-03-30 t08 Promised Land**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-03-30.141801.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 150 min [1]
- **gd1989-03-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81531.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 151 min; rated 3.44/5 by 9 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found the sound good, with some echo and booming [20]
- **gd1989-03-30.147819.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.flac24**: soundboard; 17 songs; 150 min [5]
- **gd1989-03-30.148153.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 150 min [6]
- **gd89-03-30.sennheiser-fob.ingle.10059.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 17 songs; 146 min; rated 3.38/5 by 8 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this audience recording okay and hopes a soundboard will surface [13]

## Around the show

- Jerry had guitar trouble early in the second set; it returned near the end of China Cat and the crowd reacted at once [13]
- A heavy storm, described as a mini hurricane, hit the lot a couple of hours before the show [14]
- Floor was general admission; the reviewer stood far forward and found it more intimate than the Omni in Atlanta [15]
- Reviewer snuck in through a hallway door; tried selling Becks beer, but police confiscated the roughly 20 cases [18]
- Coliseum felt like a big gymnasium; general admission floor, reviewer stood in front third on Jerry's side, with a sprawling parking lot scene [20]
- General admission floor and overnight lot camping, which was banned later that year; lot scene was in full bloom [21]
- Jerry looked and sang better than he had in a long time [21]
- A huge rainstorm swept the lot, followed by a large mushroom cloud; last spring tour allowing lot camping [22]
- Reviewer says the following night was better than this show [19]
- Reviewer calls it typical for 1989, between average and pretty good [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-03-30.141801.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100 deck, Sony ESX-HiFi/L750 tape); Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics, ortf (OTS); Transfer Info: Master PCM… [1]. Also: Ultramatrix source shnid 81531 supplies three patches in China Cat Sunflower [1]
- **gd1989-03-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81531.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [4]. Also: Audience source: Sennheiser 421 to cassette master to CD by Mark Horvath, from tapes via Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [4]
- **gd1989-03-30.147819.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.flac24**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [5]
- **gd1989-03-30.148153.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [6]
- **gd89-03-30.sennheiser-fob.ingle.10059.sbeok.shnf**: source: Mark Horvath FOB Senn. 421Âs>Sony TC-D5>MC>CDR [9]
